ai.description: *Eutropis innotata* is a small skink reaching 6 cm SVL. It is bronze-brown above with a pale lateral stripe and lacks distinct dorsal spots. Key features include a smooth-scaled body and pentadactyl limbs.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Eutropis innotata* is best distinguished by its lack of a distinct light dorsolateral stripe, which is typically present in other common Indian *Eutropis* species.
ai.habitat: *Eutropis innotata* inhabits dry deciduous forests and scrublands in peninsular India, typically found at low to moderate elevations among leaf litter and rocky outcrops.
ai.behavior: Blanford's Mabuya is a diurnal skink that actively forages for small insects among leaf litter and rocky outcrops during the warmest parts of the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Eutropis innotata* is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 3–6 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, generally between June and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Eutropis innotata* is endemic to the Indian subcontinent, primarily inhabiting the Western Ghats and parts of the Deccan Plateau across elevations up to 1,200 meters.
